summary.text: The Kepler space telescope was a NASA telescope launched in 2009 to discover Earth-sized planets orbiting other stars.
Its photometer watched star brightness, and the data were analyzed for periodic dimming caused by planets crossing in front of their stars.
It observed 530,506 stars and discovered 2,662 exoplanets over its lifetime before NASA retired it in 2018.

facts.label: Camera size
facts.value: 94.6 megapixels, largest launched into space then

items.prompt: A planet circles its star in an orbit that never takes it across the star's face as seen from Earth. What would Kepler's method do?

options.label: Detect it by its gravity pulling on the star
Detect it from heat given off by the planet
Miss it, since it only caught planets crossing the star
Detect it by photographing it directly

items.explain: Kepler looked for periodic dimming as planets cross in front of their host star, so only planets whose orbits are seen edge-on could be detected.

items.prompt: Two of Kepler's four pointing wheels failed and could not be fixed. What did NASA do next?

options.label: Approved a modified mission using the working wheels
Sent astronauts to repair the telescope
Stopped planet hunting with it altogether
Switched it to studying only supernovae

items.explain: NASA gave up fixing the two wheels, then approved the K2 extension, which used the remaining two good wheels and thrusters.

options.label: A collision with space debris
A budget cut by NASA
A failed camera sensor
Its reaction control fuel ran out

items.explain: After nine and a half years, the reaction control system fuel was depleted, and NASA announced the retirement.

items.prompt: Kepler's camera was built with a soft focus. Why?

options.label: To give sharp pictures of each planet
To measure brightness precisely rather than sharpness
To keep its sensors from overheating
To cover more sky than a sharp focus

items.explain: The photometer has a soft focus to provide excellent photometry rather than sharp images.

items.prompt: Besides planets, what else did Kepler's half-hourly brightness measurements help scientists study?

options.label: Supernovae
Comet tails
Solar flares
Black hole jets

items.explain: Measurements were collected every half-hour, so the light curves were especially useful for studying supernovae.

items.prompt: Kepler's team needed more than the planned three and a half years. What was the reason?

options.label: The telescope was launched late
The data were noisier than expected
The telescope moved too slowly
The funding had to be repaid

items.explain: Greater-than-expected noise in the data, from both the stars and the spacecraft, meant additional time was needed.
